unmapped_findings: Ms for S4 = 310 °C after austenitizing at 1250 °C, which is 5 °C higher than 305 °C measured after 1150 °C austenitization (difference within experimental scatter) [b0036, b0038, figure_005, b0088].
Bainitic transformation finish time (Bt) for S4 at TA 1250 °C / TB 350 °C = 2600 s; S4 incubation time was 50–60 s across all investigated parameters [b0057].

Product of strength and elongation (PSE) for S4 at TA 1250 °C / TB 350 °C = 11,700 MPa·% (UTS ~1410 MPa, El 8.3 %); lower than PSE of S4 at TA 1150 °C/TB 350 °C (13,380 MPa·%) and TA 1150 °C/TB 320 °C (13,600 MPa·%) [b0064].

Hardness (HV30) series reported in Fig. 7 for the eleven TA/TB conditions of S1–S5 reading left to right: 464, 497, 465, 500, 443, 457, 464, 479, 467, 459, 493 HV30; overall HV30 across alloys ranged 450–500 HV30 with higher values at lower TB except steel S4. The exact column-to-condition mapping for the S4 TA1250/TB350 column is not stated outright and is therefore not assigned as a firm value [b0061, figure_007].
S4 chemical composition (wt.%): C 0.87, Al 5.76, Mn 0.97, Si 0.30, Mo 0.48, B 0.0026, Ni 0.78, Ti 0.10 (belongs to alloy_s4 as a whole but underlies this sample) [b0018, table_001].
The 'best average and maximum elongation of 10 and 12 %' for S4 was achieved at TA 1150 °C / TB 350 °C, NOT at this sample's TA 1250 °C condition, and is therefore not attributed here [b0091].

MatCalc predicted C-dissolution temperature Tcd = 1134 °C and ferrite-free TA = 1016 °C for S4; complete dissolution of MC-type (Fe,M)xCy carbides predicted near 1134 °C for S4 [b0033, b0038, figure_004].

For S4, Ti microalloying led to coarsening of MoC into more complex TiMoC precipitates predominantly formed at temperatures above austempering; the added 1250 °C schedule dissolves nanoscale MC/TiC precipitates and partially suppresses bainitic sheaf impingement caused by small prior austenite grains at 1150 °C [b0095, b0113].
